title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
summary: A benchmark of 90 validated cases across three tool-use environments evaluated whether existing defenses covered attacks that tamper with decisions within a user’s task. Detection-and-removal reduced objective-targeting success more than observation- and state-targeting success. This is a defensive benchmark result; attack construction details are omitted.
ai_technology: Tool-using language models and detection/removal and tool-policy defenses
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: In 90 benchmark cases across three tool-use environments, detection-and-removal reduced objective-targeting success to 2.4%, while observation-targeting and state-targeting success remained 9.5% and 12.1%.
evidence.unknown: Results are benchmark-specific and do not establish operational deployment or general defense rates. Attack construction details are intentionally omitted.
evidence.ai_role: Tool-using language models and detection/removal and tool-policy defenses
